title: Anagram check
prompt: Are strings a and b anagrams (same letters, any order)?

traps.why: Strings have no sort method. Turn them into arrays, sort, and join back so === compares strings.

explanation: Sort both and compare: O(n log n). In an interview, mention the O(n) version with a 26-slot count array.
hint: Two anagrams look identical once their letters are in order.

title: Flatten one level
explanation: flat() flattens one level by default. flat(Infinity) flattens everything.
hint: There's an array method named after exactly this.

title: Group by first letter
prompt: Group words into an object keyed by first letter.
explanation: Object.groupBy (ES2024) returns { a: [...], b: [...] }. Map.groupBy does the same but returns a Map. In older runtimes, use reduce.
hint: ES2024 added a static method on Object for this.

title: All positive?
prompt: Is every number in nums greater than 0?
explanation: every stops at the first failure. Note that [].every(...) is true.
hint: some means any. Which method means all?

title: Index of the max
prompt: Get the index of the largest number in nums.
explanation: Two passes, but short and clear. A single reduce that tracks the best index does it in one pass.
hint: Find the max value first, then look up where it is.

title: Clamp
explanation: Raise x to at least lo, then cap it at hi, or the other way round.

title: Random index

traps.why: Can return n, which is out of range, and gives the two end values half as often as the others.

explanation: Math.random() is in [0, 1), so × n is in [0, n), and floor gives 0 … n − 1 evenly.
hint: Math.random() never returns 1. Which rounding keeps the result below n?

title: Map to object
prompt: Convert the Map m into a plain object.

traps.why: Spread copies an object's own properties. A Map's entries aren't properties, so you get {}.

explanation: Object.fromEntries takes any iterable of [key, value] pairs, and a Map is one. Going back: new Map(Object.entries(obj)).
hint: A Map iterates as [key, value] pairs. Which Object method accepts those?

title: Sleep
prompt: A promise that resolves after ms milliseconds.
explanation: Pass resolve straight to setTimeout. Then await sleep(500) pauses an async function.
hint: Wrap setTimeout in new Promise. What should the timer call?

title: Two-digit padding
prompt: Format the number n as two digits: 5 → '05'.

traps.why: padStart is a string method, and n is a number. Convert it first.

explanation: padStart(length, fill) pads on the left up to the target length. Handy for clocks and dates.
hint: Convert to a string first, then pad on the left.
